national_raw_news.content: India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into force from 20th of October this year. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the Agreement provides duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. He said, the strategic partnerships reflects the shared ambition to deepen this cooperation and aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to almost 35 thousand crore rupees in the next 4 to 5 years. This will open new opportunities for Indian exports including textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and processed food products. At the same time, New Zealand will gain enhanced and access to the Indian market for products including wood, wool, sheep meat, and raw leather hides. The Agreement also creates new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students. It provides for facilitating 20 billion US dollars of investment into India and strengthens bilateral cooperation in areas including agricultural productivity, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, traditional medicine and AYUSH, technology and trade facilitation. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 74 Vladimir Putin’s United Russia Party retains majority in Parliament
national_raw_news.content: Russian Central Election Commission said that the ruling United Russia party has won 57.83 per cent of the votes in the election for the 9th State Duma, the lower house of parliament. The results will help President Vladimir Putin maintain his tight grip on power. Addressing a press conference in Moscow today, Russian Central Election Commission Chairperson Ella Pamfilova said that after 95.18 per cent of the ballots were counted, United Russia led with 57.83 per cent of the vote, followed by the Communist Party of the Russian Federation with 13.81 per cent and the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia with 8.98 per cent. New People garnered 7.96 per cent and A Just Russia 4.96 per cent of the votes. According to the CEC, turnout in this election, held from Friday to Sunday, was 59.32 per cent, higher than the 51.72 per cent in 2021. The State Duma is Russia’s permanent legislative body, composed of 450 deputies. Half of the seats are distributed proportionally in accordance with party lists, while the remaining 225 are elected through single-mandate constituencies nationwide under a relative-majority voting system. A total of 10 political parties participated in the election. The final results are expected to be announced on Friday. It was the first parliamentary election after Russian military operation in Ukraine in 2022. Pamfilova criticised Western leaders and institutions for groundlessly smearing Russia’s elections.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Sports 87 Asian Games: India win three medals in shooting at Aichi-Nagoya; PM Modi Congratulates Medal Winners
national_raw_news.content: India won three medals in shooting at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today. In the men’s 10-meter air rifle individual event, Himanshu Dhillon won the silver medal, while Rudrankksh Patil secured the bronze. India also bagged a silver medal in the men’s team event of the same competition. Yesterday, Elavenil Valarivan won the silver medal in the women’s individual 10-metre air rifle event. India also bagged a silver medal in the women’s team event of the same competition. With this, India has won a total of five medals in Shooting so far, including four silver and one bronze. Suchika Tariyal has become the first athlete from the country to win a medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA). Suchika secured the bronze medal in the 60 kg category. In the medal tally, India is currently in 12th place with a total of six medals, including four silver and two bronze. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Himanshu Dhillon, and Parth Rakesh Mane on winning the silver medal in the Men’s 10 meter Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr. Modi commended the trio, stating that their focus, consistency, and exceptional teamwork have made the entire nation proud. In addition to the team success, the Prime Minister lauded the athletes for their individual achievements in the Men’s 10 meter Air Rifle event. Congratulating Himanshu Dhillon on winning the silver medal, Mr Modi praised his composure and remarkable accuracy under pressure, noting that his performance was a source of national pride. Extending his congratulations to Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil for securing the bronze medal, Mr Modi appreciated his focus and discipline throughout the competition, wishing him continued success in all his future endeavors.

national_raw_news.title: UP CM Yogi Adityanath Calls Upon Party Workers to Work for Society with Nation First Approach 2 hours ago 27
national_raw_news.content: BJP National President Nitin Nabin, along with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, today reviewed the party’s organisational preparations for the upcoming Assembly elections in Meerut. During the review meeting, preparations were assessed at the booth, Shakti Kendra, Mandal and district levels. Mr Nabin, who is on a two-day visit to Western Uttar Pradesh, also interacted directly with party workers. Uttar Pradesh BJP President and Union Minister of State Pankaj Chaudhary was also present. The meeting discussed the organisational position, preparations for the forthcoming elections and feedback received from the grassroots. Addressing a conference of Shakti Kendra convenors, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath called upon party workers to work for society with a sense of putting the nation first. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the world is witnessing a new India. He said that since Narendra Modi assumed the office of Prime Minister in 2014, India has emerged as a new India-one that takes pride in its heritage while maintaining the momentum of development. He added that India no longer faces an identity crisis and that its economy has moved from the bottom five to the top five globally. BJP National President Nitin Nabin described Meerut as the land of revolution. Referring to the transformation witnessed in Uttar Pradesh over the past nine-and-a-half years, he said that the state today has an atmosphere of trust, the rule of law and is progressing on the path of development. Mr Nabin also interacted with young people and described the youth as one of the country’s current strengths. The BJP National President will visit Saharanpur tomorrow, where he is scheduled to hold a meeting with MPs, MLAs, district-level office bearers and former office bearers.
